analysis.title: Deep Water-Filled Pothole in Travel Lane on Park Ave
analysis.summary: A resident reports a pothole roughly two feet wide in the right travel lane of Park Ave near Chandler St. Standing water hides its depth, and drivers are swerving into the adjacent lane to avoid it.
analysis.reasoning: A concealed pothole in an active travel lane on a busy arterial creates collision and tire-damage risk, and lane swerving endangers other vehicles.
analysis.recommended_action: Dispatch a DPW crew to cold-patch within 48 hours and schedule a permanent hot-mix repair.

analysis.title: Streetlight Out on Shrewsbury St Pedestrian Route
analysis.summary: A streetlight near the Washington Square rotary on Shrewsbury St has been dark for over a week. The sidewalk is unlit at night on a route pedestrians use to and from Union Station.
analysis.reasoning: An unlit sidewalk on a well-used pedestrian route raises personal-safety and traffic risk after dark.
analysis.recommended_action: Submit a repair ticket to the utility and inspect the fixture and photocell within 72 hours.

analysis.title: Root-Heaved Sidewalk Slabs Near Clark University
analysis.summary: Sidewalk slabs on Main St near Clark University are lifted several inches by tree roots. The resident reports trip incidents and says strollers and wheelchairs cannot pass.
analysis.reasoning: Vertical displacement of several inches is a trip hazard and an ADA accessibility barrier on a busy pedestrian corridor near a campus.
analysis.recommended_action: Mark the hazard, grind or ramp the displaced edges now, and schedule slab replacement with a root barrier.

analysis.title: Furniture and Trash Bags Dumped at Providence St Park Entrance
analysis.summary: A mattress, a couch and several trash bags were dumped at the end of Providence St by the park entrance. The pile has been there since the weekend and is producing odor.
analysis.reasoning: Bulky dumped items at a park entrance attract pests and further dumping, and block part of the access path.
analysis.recommended_action: Schedule a bulk-item pickup within the week and check for evidence to support code enforcement.

analysis.title: Large Graffiti on Major Taylor Blvd Underpass Wall
analysis.summary: Spray-painted graffiti covers a large section of the underpass wall on Major Taylor Blvd. The resident notes that some of the content is offensive.
analysis.reasoning: Graffiti is not a safety hazard, but offensive content in a high-visibility location warrants prompt removal.
analysis.recommended_action: Assign the graffiti removal crew; prioritize removing offensive content within 48 hours.

analysis.title: Clogged Storm Drain Flooding Lincoln St Intersection
analysis.summary: The storm drain at Lincoln St and Burncoat St is clogged, and the intersection floods ankle-deep after every rain. Vehicles are slowing to drive through the water.
analysis.reasoning: Recurring standing water at an intersection creates hydroplaning risk, blocks crosswalks, and will freeze in cold weather.
analysis.recommended_action: Send a vactor truck to clear the catch basin and inspect the outlet pipe for blockage.

analysis.title: Graffiti Reported as Pothole on Grafton St
analysis.summary: The resident describes a large pothole on Grafton St, but the attached photo shows spray-painted graffiti on a wall with no visible road damage. The report has been classified from the photo.
analysis.reasoning: Scores reflect the graffiti shown in the photo; the described pothole could not be verified from the image.
analysis.recommended_action: Route to the graffiti removal crew and ask the resident to confirm whether a pothole is also present.
analysis.mismatch_note: The description claims a pothole, but the photo shows graffiti on a wall and no road surface damage.
